text:
maria-sales: Quick sync — GlimmerHealth POC perf run just finished and we're seeing a weird tail at ~200 qps, p95 ~= 420ms but p99 spikes to 1.8s. Anyone around to triage?

sam: I'm free, sending initial notes. Did you run with KV prefix cache enabled? That usually affects tail.

maria-sales: Yes we ran with prefix cache enabled and batching at target 8. Warmup for 10m.

sam: Can you paste the exact load command and model+seq config?

maria-sales: Load harness: `vegeta attack -rate=200 -duration=10m -targets=glimmer_targets.txt | vegeta report` Model: `redwood/gpt-small-quant` max_seq=512, avg_output_tokens=60, batching=8, token_cache=prefix (enabled).

ben: Quick note from infra: during the window the nodes had a noisy neighbor causing CPU steal around 12:14 UTC — I saw a 7% steal on one host. Could account for some spikes. We'll validate host-level metrics.

sam: OK — let's isolate variables. Plan: 1) Re-run short experiments toggling prefix cache on/off; 2) run with batching=1 to see baseline latency per-token; 3) compare model variant `redwood/gpt-small-quant` vs `redwood/gpt-small-int8` to check kernel differences; 4) capture rt breakdown (queueing, compute, network).

anya: Thx. Also need a quick note for GlimmerHealth on how this affects pricing — if we need to drop batching to reduce tail, what's cost delta? Rough ballpark is fine.

sam: Rough ballpark: batching drop from 8->1 increases token unit cost ~3.5x for this workload due to lost batching efficiency. We'll quantify after runs.

ops-bot: Deploy notice: canary nodes for runtime rolled at 2026-03-20T12:00Z to runtime-v2.3.1 (no config changes).

ben: For the runs, use this vegeta target template to simulate realistic prompt lengths (mix 40/80/120 token prompts):

```
POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
Content-Type: application/json

{"model":"redwood/gpt-small-quant","input":"<PROMPT>","max_tokens":60}
```

Include header `X-Redwood-Test: glimmer-poc` to filter in logs.

sam: I'll own the re-runs. Quick helper command to collect per-request timing with curl+jq in parallel (small script):

```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -w '%{time_starttransfer}\n' -X POST ... &
done | sort -n | tail -n 20
```

maria-sales: Running toggles now. One quick ask — security asked if we touched their encrypted payloads (HSM/KMS) during POC. We used customer-supplied key for logging obfuscation only, no KMS wrap at inference path.

anya: I'll note that for the questionnaire. Also Glimmer wants an ETA for a short write-up comparing p95/p99 across configs. Can we have a concise summary in ~24h?

sam: Yes — I expect initial summary with charts within 24h. Early findings (prelim): turning prefix cache off reduced p99 from 1.8s -> ~1.1s but increased p50 by ~10ms due to missed reuse. Disabling batching gave p50 ~95ms but p99 stayed ~1.0-1.2s likely due to queue head-of-line.

ben: Infrastructure follow-ups: we'll move that noisy host out of the pool and re-run a sanity sweep to ensure no host-level contention.

maria-sales: Nice. Can you also capture token counts and CPU/GPU utilization per run? Glimmer cares about unit economics and worst-case latency under burst.

sam: Yep. I'll gather: per-token cost estimate, p50/p95/p99, KV hit rate, avg batch size, GPU util, and a short recommendation: suggested config for production (batching=4, prefix_cache=on, model=`redwood/gpt-small-int8`) and fallback policy (auto-fallback to lower batch when p95 > 300ms).

anya: Perfect. I'll prep a one-pager with the cost delta options: conservative (batch=1), balanced (batch=4), aggressive (batch=8) so sales can include numbers in the quote.

ops-bot: Load test run started by @sam at 2026-03-21T09:14Z (run id glimmer-1719999000-1).

sam: Posting quick raw numbers from the first toggle run (kv cache ON vs OFF, batching=8):
- kv=ON: p50 88ms, p95 420ms, p99 1.8s, kv_hit=72%, avg_batch=7.9
- kv=OFF: p50 98ms, p95 360ms, p99 1.1s, kv_hit=0%, avg_batch=7.8

sam: Follow-up run batching=1 (kv OFF): p50 95ms, p95 340ms, p99 1.05s, cost_est ~= 3.6x tokens/second cost.

ben: After moving noisy host, re-run results look cleaner: p99 with kv ON dropped to 950ms on stable infra. So host contention was big factor.

maria-sales: Great signal — can you distill into a 1-paragraph summary I can send to the Glimmer stakeholders? Also include recommended config and short pricing delta table.

sam: Draft summary: "We observed elevated p99 during initial runs caused by a combination of prefix-cache interaction and transient host contention. On stable hosts, p99 trims to ~950ms with prefix cache enabled and batching=8. If you prioritize tighter tail SLOs, we recommend batching=4 with prefix cache enabled and model variant `redwood/gpt-small-int8` — this gives ~p95 280-320ms and p99 ~700-900ms with an estimated 1.8x cost vs aggressive batching=8. We will include exact cost numbers in the follow-up."

anya: That's perfect. I'll attach that to the Glimmer health-check email and schedule a 30-min tech review.

maria-sales: Thanks team. Assigning owners: sam -> perf runs & write-up, ben -> infra sweep, anya -> price sheet & stakeholder sync. Closing thread once write-up posted. :thumbsup:
